threat_scenario: RollJam: jam + capture the first code, replay it later to open the vehicle
attack_path: Attacker near the vehicle with a transmit/receive SDR; on the owner's lock press, jam the 433 MHz band and capture the code (vehicle receives nothing, stays unlocked); on the second press, jam+capture again and replay the first code (vehicle locks, owner leaves); replay the retained second code later to open the vehicle (accepted within the F-05 look-ahead window, A-05)
feasibility_rationale: Consumer SDR (e.g. HackRF, ~300EUR), published technique (RollJam, 2015); requires presence when the owner locks (window of opportunity); relies on A-05 (tolerant look-ahead window)

threat_scenario: Denial jamming: jam the 433 MHz band during the lock command so the BCM receives nothing and the vehicle stays unlocked while the owner believes it is locked
attack_path: Attacker positioned near a parked vehicle, within radio range (`01` §5), with an off-the-shelf 433 MHz jammer; when the owner presses the key-fob lock button, the attacker jams the band so the BCM receives no frame and the doors stay unlocked; the attack succeeds only if the owner leaves without checking the lock-confirmation feedback (no indicator flash is possible, since the BCM did not lock); the attacker then accesses the unlocked vehicle
feasibility_rationale: Opportunistic radio attack, no physical access. Elapsed time: low (immediate setup). Expertise: Layman. Knowledge of the item: public (jamming is well documented). Equipment: Standard (off-the-shelf 433 MHz jammer, simpler than the TS-01 SDR). Window of opportunity: Moderate (many lock events in a public car park, but each attempt needs the exact lock instant and an owner who does not verify the feedback). By the §4 access-means mapping this rates High; see the §4 scale limitation on the window not being separately weighted.

threat_scenario: Pair an attacker key via OBD diagnostic, then open the vehicle with it
attack_path: Attacker with temporary authorized access to the vehicle and its key fob (valet / rental / workshop); using an OBD-II diagnostic tool plugged into the in-cabin port (`01` A-03), the attacker invokes the key-pairing service F-03, routed through the gateway to the BCM (I-05 then I-04), and enrols an additional attacker-controlled key; the vehicle is returned, and the attacker later opens it at will with the enrolled key (persistent covert access)
feasibility_rationale: Temporary authorized access (valet / rental / workshop), limited physical access via the in-cabin OBD port (`01` A-03). Elapsed time: low, <=1 day (pairing is quick once access is obtained). Expertise: Proficient (requires knowing the diagnostic key-pairing procedure). Knowledge of the item: Restricted (the pairing procedure is service/workshop-restricted, not public). Window of opportunity: Moderate (such access situations occur, but each attempt needs the attacker unobserved while connecting the tool and able to locate the vehicle again later). Equipment: Specialized (a diagnostic tool able to run the key-pairing routine). By the §4 access-means mapping this rates Medium (OBD access inside the cabin).
